NodeConformance.__comment: Disabled by default. Enabling the local-only L0 descriptor requires a durable dedicated node-identity directory and a read-only metadata-bound CI artifact bundle for G1/G2/G3/G5/G7. ExpectedRepository and ExpectedWorkflow must exactly match trusted CI; the running assembly revision must match metadata. This does not activate federation, a DHT, peers, or any wallet capability.

NodeTransparencyHistory.__comment: Disabled by default. This signed public checkpoint uses the dedicated NodeConformance identity and its protected durable directory; it never enables federation, paid egress, or value settlement.

Auth.__comment: Federated sign-in (Phase 1B). Client secrets are host-managed write-only credentials supplied at deploy time as Auth__Google__ClientSecret / Auth__GitHub__ClientSecret and must NEVER be committed. Setting a provider's Enabled=true without both its ClientId and ClientSecret is a HARD STARTUP FAILURE (Services/Auth/ExternalAuthRuntimeSafety.cs) rather than a sign-in button that 500s on first use.

NodeOperator.__comment: Seed-only node authority. Supply Username, Password, and a positive monotonic CredentialRevision together through the host secret store. The password is hashed before persistence and is never returned. Production refuses a first launch without a complete seed; later launches may use the durable binding. SessionMinutes must be 5-30.

AdminBootstrap.__comment: Legacy compatibility only; do not use for new nodes. Both SeedEmail and SeedSecret must be set together if an existing deployment still carries this seam. New node authority is configured under NodeOperator.

AZOA.__platformKeyComment: Platform signing keys are PER CHAIN: each chain's key is derived from its own secret by its own rule (Services/Custody/PlatformKeyDerivations.cs). A chain with no registered derivation fails closed naming that chain — it is never derived by another chain's rule. Blank here on purpose: supply real values per environment (env vars / appsettings.<Environment>.json / the deploy secret store), never in this file. Every chain ENABLED under Blockchain:Chains must have its key set or the real-value readiness probe fails.

KycCallback.__comment: Own budget for the unauthenticated provider callback; its shared secret rides in the body, so it must not draw on the anonymous global allowance.

FiatWebhook.__comment: Own budget for the unauthenticated payment webhook; its authority is the signature on the body, so it must not draw on the anonymous global allowance. Set this too low and a legitimate provider retry burst is rejected with a 429 the provider counts as a failed delivery -- a person charged with nothing credited.

ActionDefinition.__comment: Marketplace run-start quota (Managers/AGENTS.md §action-run-quota). MaxRunsPerUserPerAction caps a NON-owner's concurrent non-terminal runs of one action (treasury/runner-drain guard); <=0 disables. OwnerLimitMultiplier scales the ceiling for the owner running their OWN action; <=0 exempts the owner.

Kyc.__comment: Provider credentials are host-managed write-only secrets. Identomat is the node default: the adapter reports UNAVAILABLE until Kyc__Identomat__* secrets are supplied at deploy time, so naming it here selects the policy without ever pretending it is configured. The operator dashboard changes secret-free provider policy only.

Identomat.__comment: Credential NAMES only. CompanyKey / ConfigId / CallbackApiKey are supplied at deploy time as Kyc__Identomat__CompanyKey, Kyc__Identomat__ConfigId, Kyc__Identomat__CallbackApiKey and must never be committed. Two base URLs is not a mistake: /begin and all AML screening live on the camelCase external-api host, while the authoritative /result/ lives on the legacy snake_case widget host.
Identomat.__return_url_comment: Where the hosted widget sends the applicant when they finish. /begin has NO top-level redirect parameter; the only documented one is the per-session general.returnUrl override, which is what this key populates. Must be a public HTTPS URL (loopback and private address space are refused) or it is dropped and nothing is sent. Empty = leave the dashboard configuration alone.
Identomat.__rate_comment: ONE shared per-IP budget across KYC session calls, AML screening, and monitor polls. The vendor bans the IP for an hour past 600/min, so the default leaves headroom rather than racing the ceiling.
Identomat.__replica_comment: SharedRequestsPerMinute and TenantQuota are NODE-WIDE numbers enforced by a PER-PROCESS counter. ReplicaCount divides them down, so N replicas behind one egress IP still spend one node's allowance instead of N. Raise it to the real replica count before scaling out, or the vendor IP ban this budget exists to prevent is exactly what scaling out causes.

Screening.__comment: There is no APPROVED/REJECTED enum on the screening surface; every band here is an AZOA operator decision. BlockingTopics is an OPEN string set, not a closed enum, because the vendor publishes no exhaustive topic list.
Screening.__search_paging_comment: The search response carries no total and no documented sort order, so an unpaged read silently drops every hit past the first window and cannot tell a clean subject from a saturated one. SearchMaxPages bounds the walk; saturating it marks the result truncated, which is forced to manual review and never reads as a pass.

TenantQuota.__comment: Per-tenant ceiling in front of the shared node budget. Without it one consumer's begin-session storm exhausts the node-wide per-IP allowance and evicts every other tenant from KYC.

Identity.__comment: PersonKeySecret is supplied at deploy time as Kyc__Identity__PersonKeySecret (>= 32 chars) and must never be committed. It is the HKDF root from which every PER-TENANT person-key salt is derived, so one human resolves to an unlinkable key in each tenant. Rotating it re-pseudonymises every existing binding.
Identity.__retention_sweep_comment: retention_expires_at is written on kyc_identity, kyc_screening_result, and kyc_screening_monitor. KycIdentityRetentionSweepWorker is what makes it more than decoration; it issues no vendor calls, so it has no rate-budget cost and needs no opt-in.

ApprovalPolicy.__comment: The reviewed trust profile the node stamps onto every approval. These are NODE policy, never tenant policy. PolicyVersion and AssuranceLevel are exact-match labels: changing either invalidates existing approvals and forces re-verification, which is the intended lever when the reviewed flow changes. TrustedProviderKeys is the set of identity authorities the operator accepts.

Kyc.__expiry_comment: Two different clocks. SubmissionExpiryDays bounds how long an UNFINISHED attempt may sit before it is abandoned. ApprovalValidityDays is how long a granted APPROVAL stays current; stamping an approval with the submission clock forces every verified sponsor back through identity check a month later.

TenantProviderOverride.__comment: The KYC provider a tenant verifies through IS that tenant's compliance policy, so PUT /api/tenant/kyc/provider is OFF for every tenant by default. Both keys must agree: this switch AND the tenant's id on AllowedTenantIds. The operator's own route (PUT /api/nodeoperator/tenants/{id}/kyc-provider) is never gated by this. "*" admits every tenant and should be a deliberate, audited choice.

Registration.__comment: POST /api/user/register is [AllowAnonymous]. Enabled=false refuses it on any host. In Production it is refused regardless unless AllowPublicSelfServiceInProduction is ALSO true, so a node that inherits this file verbatim never opens anonymous account creation by accident. Operator-provisioned tenants and their child users are unaffected.

Reserve.__comment: The platform reserve is the operator-owned custodial account that holds the platform unit and every project asset, is the manager/reserve/freeze/clawback authority on the assets this node creates, and pays the chain fees. It has NO secret of its own: its key is the per-chain platform key under AZOA:<Chain>:PlatformMnemonic, so a chain whose platform key is missing resolves no reserve address at all rather than one this node cannot sign for. See docs/NODE-HOST.md section 8.11.
Reserve.__chainsComment: Chains the reserve may operate on. A reserve operation on a chain absent from a NON-EMPTY list is refused before any key is touched. An empty list means no restriction.
Reserve.__fungibleMintTargetComment: PlatformReserve (default) makes the reserve the creator and the holder of all four ASA authorities, and opens the asset's reserve ledger row. CallerWallet is the legacy shape and cannot broadcast on Algorand: an ASA-create is signed with the platform key, so a create whose sender is the caller's custodial wallet has a sender the signature does not match. Do not use it outside a simulated chain.
Reserve.__expectedAddressesComment: Optional operator assertion, per chain. When an entry is present and non-blank, the address DERIVED from that chain's platform key must equal it exactly or every reserve operation on that chain fails closed. This is how a swapped or mistyped mnemonic is caught at first use instead of after value has moved. Blank here on purpose: fill it in per environment once the reserve address is known and independently verified.
Reserve.__feePayerComment: Reserved for a future dedicated fee-payer account. No separate fee-payer key exists, so the reserve itself pays fees and this must stay false.
Reserve.__platformUnitDrawComment: OI-21. The node's OWN unit carries no tenant on its reserve ledger row because the node minted it, so 'no tenant on the row' means 'the operator's', never 'anybody's'. This setting says who ELSE may draw its declared partitions: OperatorOnly (narrowest), DeclaredTenants (only the ids in PlatformUnitDrawTenants), or AnyAdmittedTenant (any tenant this node resolved from an operator-issued value-scoped principal). OperatorOnly is the default and an unrecognised value fails closed, so a node that says nothing keeps its own supply to its own rails. Under EVERY value a caller with no resolvable tenant at all is refused, which is the shape a user-driven action run arrives in.

Fiat.__comment: The Fiat.USD value rail (W4.1): card money in through a hosted payment page. Secrets are host-managed write-only credentials supplied at deploy time as Fiat__Test__SecretKey / Fiat__Test__WebhookSecret (and the Live__ pair) and must NEVER be committed. Enabling the rail without the selected environment's secret key, its webhook secret, or a return-origin allowlist is a HARD STARTUP FAILURE (FiatRailStartup.Validate in Providers/Fiat/FiatRailProvider.cs), not an Add-funds button that fails on first use.
Fiat.__environmentComment: test or live; nothing else parses. ONE environment binds at a time, so a test-mode checkout can never be settled by a live webhook inside one process. Setting it to live additionally refuses to boot while Blockchain:Mode is Simulated, or while no IFiatSettlementHandler is registered -- charging a real card with nothing able to credit it is the worst failure this rail has.
Fiat.__toleranceComment: Replay tolerance on the webhook signature timestamp. The timestamp is part of the signed material, so a captured delivery cannot be replayed once it falls outside this window.
Fiat.__chargebackComment: How long after a cleared card payment a reversal can still arrive. This is the rail's SettlementProfile window -- what any hold placed against on-ramped funds computes its release time from. 120 days is the card-scheme worst case; shortening it shortens the protection, not the risk.
Fiat.__onRampComment: W4.2 -- what a cleared payment turns into. ReservePartition names the platform-reserve partition on-ramp issuance draws from; it MUST be declared on the reserve ledger (IPlatformReserve.DeclarePartitionsAsync) before the first real payment. AllowNodeDefaultScheduleFallback stays false so a tenant with no registered price schedule cannot be sold units at a node-wide default price -- register one via POST /api/fiat/price-schedule instead. Every key here has a fail-closed default, so the section may be omitted; it is spelled out so an operator can see the settings rather than discover them.
Fiat.__reversalComment: W4.3 -- what a refund or chargeback unwinds. Every default is fail-safe, so an absent section is a working configuration. AbsorbAtOrBelowMinorUnits 0 means nothing is ever written off silently. RecoverOnDisputeOpened stays false because a dispute is not yet a loss: the account is flagged and the units are left alone until the dispute is actually lost. Per-flow overrides go in Flows, keyed by flow name.
Fiat.__offRampComment: W8.1 -- the other half of the money path: units become money in a person's bank account, paid out through the same provider's Connect payouts. Every default is fail-closed, so an ABSENT section is a working configuration in which cashing out simply reports that it is not available -- it never half-works. Enabling it REQUIRES both onboarding URLs, and each must itself satisfy Fiat:Checkout:AllowedReturnOrigins: an unbounded return URL on an identity-verification page is the same open redirect the checkout page guards against. ReservePartition names the platform-reserve partition a cash-out is drawn back into and should match OnRamp:ReservePartition unless an operator deliberately separates them. The bounds are on MONEY in minor units; the units debited are derived from them, never the other way round.

Checkout.__originsComment: Origins (scheme://host[:port]) a success or cancel URL may point at. Scheme, host and port must ALL match an entry. An EMPTY list blocks every checkout and fails boot while the rail is enabled: an unbounded return URL on a payment page is an open redirect a phisher can aim at their own copy of the site, on the one page where a person has just typed their card number. A non-https origin is refused outright in the live environment; plain http is tolerated only for loopback outside it.
Checkout.__purposesComment: Routing values a caller may name. An EMPTY list allows NOTHING -- it is deliberately not read as 'unrestricted', which is how the retired sidecar turned a forgotten key into an open dimension -- and fails boot while the rail is enabled.
Checkout.__amountComment: Bounds on one payment, in minor units of Currency. These bound the MONEY a person pays; the units they receive are derived at webhook time from the provider-confirmed amount, never from anything a client sent.
Checkout.__productNameComment: The line-item label the payer sees. Keep it in the vocabulary of money: it must never name a unit, an asset, or a chain.
Checkout.__returnUrlComment: Used when a caller supplies none. Must itself satisfy AllowedReturnOrigins. The rail appends an intent query parameter so the return page can find the payment it came back to.

__exchangeComment: The treasury-rate exchange (W5.1). Every key here has a fail-closed default, so the section may be omitted; it is spelled out so an operator can see the settings rather than discover them. MaxDeclaredRateAge non-positive REFUSES every exchange -- it is never read as 'no limit'.

Exchange.__rateBandComment: OI-81 -- both bounds are the OPERATOR'S DECLARATION of what one platform base unit is worth in the quoted asset's minor units. This is a band over the platform unit's declared value, not over a peg: the unit is backing-derived and drifts, so a fixed peg would refuse every honest rate. A blank or inverted band refuses EVERY declared rate rather than admitting any -- widening the band is the operator's visible act, blanking it is not a shortcut. Pinning the unit to one value means narrowing BOTH bounds, not just one. RateConsistencyDustMinorUnits is the rounding slack a round-trip may lose before the pair is called inconsistent.
Exchange.__settlementComment: Durable exchange settlement -- MaximumGroupNetworkFeeBaseUnits is the reserve's accepted cap on one atomic group's pooled network fee in the rail's native base units (blank refuses every exchange); UnsentSourceAbandonAfter returns the commitment of an exchange that was committed but never authorized for transmission once idle that long; MaximumRecipientFundingBaseUnits caps the native units the reserve advances inside the same atomic group so a participant can accept what a direct purchase or sale delivers ("0" funds nothing and refuses an unready account).
Exchange.__buyBackComment: W8.2 -- what makes SELLING possible at all. The rate policy refuses every sell unless a liquidity policy is registered AND admits it; Enabled false keeps it refusing even once registered, so turning this on is a deliberate operator act. A sell is paid from the PROJECT's own treasury first; BackstopPartition is a declared platform-reserve partition, not a movement, and must be declared on the reserve ledger before the first backstopped sell. When the treasury is short, QueueEnabled parks the seller in a head-of-line FIFO with a stated place rather than failing them; MaxUnitsPerRequest empty means the share-of-treasury cap is the only per-request bound.

GuardianSets.__comment: Config-driven Wormhole Guardian sets consumed by Secp256k1VaaSignatureVerifier. Key = Guardian-set index (string, the VAA header GuardianSetIndex). Value = ORDERED list of 0x-prefixed 20-byte Ethereum-style Guardian addresses; list position == Guardian index. INTENTIONALLY NO testnet/mainnet entries here: an absent set fails closed (no VAA can be verified — see Secp256k1VaaSignatureVerifier). Do NOT add placeholder/guessed addresses. Real testnet/mainnet sets must be supplied + independently verified per the per-environment procedure in conductor/tracks/api-safety-hardening/GUARDIAN-SET-SETUP.md, dropped into the matching appsettings.<Environment>.json under this same Blockchain:Wormhole:GuardianSets key. appsettings.Development.json carries the verified devnet (tilt) set, index 0.
